reference.notes: The stand is named only through the machine-translated transcript ('the snack is called the cell'), so the name is kept as 'The Cell'. The transcript is hard to follow, so the owner's statements about his technique (temperature, tomatoes) are kept as facts about the place.

match.note: The kebab stand 'The Cell' (Die Zelle) is not among the candidates; the closest names (Cello Cafe, Castell, etc.) are different venues.

revisions.note: claims.extra (both_ok): The kebab turning liquid can be kept as its own claim or folded into the tomato claim.
parts.sentiment (both_ok): Splitting out the flat tomato as a negative judgement of the ingredient is a reasonable reading.
parts.kind (both_ok): The tomatoes becoming crappy can be read as an opinion in the agent's split.
parts.kind (both_ok): The agent's split claim judges the tomatoes, so opinion is defensible.
parts.sentiment (both_ok): A negative sentiment fits the split claim that the tomatoes were flat or crappy.
